subject: Consumption friction & term alignment for Q4 renewal
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Cook <avery@lumen.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Consumption friction & term alignment for Q4 renewal

Hi Avery / Nora —

Attached is a short snapshot of your Q3 consumption pattern (lumen_q3_usage.csv) and a small latency spot-check (latency_spotcheck_sep01.pdf). Quick summary up front:

- Token consumption has flattened over the last 6 weeks despite a ~8% increase in active users. The top 3 endpoints account for ~62% of calls.
- We see concentrated latency variance on long-generation paths (median tail around 350ms, spikes past 1s during the 10–11am PT window).
- Economics: your mix is skewed toward high-context prompts; a modest reduction in avg tokens/request (even ~10%) materially changes month-to-month unit costs.

Questions I want to align on before the renewal conversation next month:
1) Would you be open to a short 3-month term extension while we run a targeted performance experiment (prefix caching + batching) to reduce tokens per request and stabilize latency?
2) If we can demonstrate >10% token reduction across the three heavy endpoints, would you consider a tiered commit that increases reserved capacity at lower unit price?

Proposed next steps:
- Solutions sync: Marcus to validate feasibility and expected token savings (ETA 48h).
- Ops: show a Console dashboard for per-route latency and token mix (So that product/ops can track progress).
- Commercial: Kimberly to outline a short extension + burst credit offer we can put on the table for the renewal.

If that sounds reasonable I can draft a mutual action plan and schedule a 30-min sync. Available times: today 3–5pm PT or tomorrow morning.

Thanks —
Jonas
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: lumen_q3_usage.csv (summary), latency_spotcheck_sep01.pdf (sample traces)

Subject: Re: Consumption friction & term alignment for Q4 renewal

Jonas —

Thanks for the snapshot and the suggested path. We’ve been worried about the long-tail latency on our summarization pipeline; ops flagged it last week when a customer-facing job timed out. I forwarded logs to your team (see attached: app_logs_0831.zip) — they show a few thousand long-chain prompts that look like they could benefit from better KV caching.

A couple of constraints on our side:
- Budget cadence is fixed for Q4; we can’t commit to a meaningful uplift without a clear ROI case.
- We can run experiments but only if they don’t require gateway changes in our infra (would prefer config toggles or a Redwood-side optimization).

Ask: can Marcus confirm if the prefix/KV cache work is something Redwood can enable without SDK/infra changes? Also, can you provide an estimate of token savings and the expected delta in $/1M tokens if we move a fraction of traffic to a quantized variant you mentioned at the kickoff?

If we can get a short-term offer (3 months) that includes burst credits and a documented measurement plan, I think we can present that to our finance/ops.

Avery asked two explicit things: (1) can we enable prefix/KV caching without infra changes on their side; (2) provide an estimate of token savings and $/1M token delta for quantized variant.

Marcus — can you confirm feasibility and give a conservative estimate for token savings for the three heavy endpoints? Key constraints: no gateway changes (prefer server-side config) and minimal client rollout. If you need a dev session with their infra team, say so and I’ll book it.

Kimberly — if we can show >=10% token reduction, what short-term commercial packaging can we offer (3-month extension + X burst credits + staggered commit)? Please include a fallback (no-penalty exit) clause we can propose if the experiment fails to reach the threshold.

Soojin — can you prep a shareable Console view (per-route token mix, avg tokens per request, tail latency) and the dashboard link we can pass to the customer? We’ll want to track week-over-week change.

I’ve attached a quick savings_estimate_calculation.xlsx with a baseline and two scenarios (10% and 15% reduction). Use conservative numbers for capacity headroom.

Goal: come back to Avery with a one-page mutual action plan and an offer by 11:30am PT so we can schedule the exec review this afternoon.

Thanks —
Jonas

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Consumption friction & term alignment for Q4 renewal — mutual action plan

Avery / Nora —

Thanks for the quick reply and the logs. Per our internal check-in here’s a concise mutual action plan and a commercial bridge we can put forward.

Mutual action plan (short pilot + measured outcome)- Objective: reduce avg tokens/request across three heavy endpoints by >=10% and reduce tail latency in the 10–11am PT window.
- Timeline: enable Redwood-side prefix/KV caching config (no infra changes) — 48h to roll-on; 2-week measurement window.
- Measurement: Console dashboard (per-route token mix + tail latency) that we’ll share live. Soojin will send the dashboard link.
- Success threshold: >=10% reduction in avg tokens/request for the combined sample across three endpoints.

Commercial bridge (3-month extension offer)- Term: 3 months extension from current renewal date with a staged commit add-on: +20% reserved capacity priced at a 12% unit-rate discount (applies only if success threshold met).
- Burst credits: 200k free token credits usable anytime in the 3-month window.
- Fallback: if the pilot fails to reach the threshold, the extension terminates at original renewal date with no penalty and we credit 50k tokens as a consolation.

Estimated economics (conservative)
- Baseline avg monthly tokens: 18M
- Scenario A (10% reduction): saves ~1.8M tokens/mo -> estimated $1,150/mo in gross spend reduction (ballpark; final will depend on your token mix).
- Scenario B (15% reduction): saves ~2.7M tokens/mo -> ~ $1,700/mo savings. (Detailed calc in attached spreadsheet.)

Next steps
1) Marcus to confirm caching toggle and expected engineering effort by EOD today.
2) Soojin will share the Console dashboard link for week 0 baseline.
3) Kimberly to send a short-term contract addendum (3 pages max) with the staged commit and burst credits.
4) Book a 30-minute review with your finance/ops — here’s my Calendly: https://calendly.com/redwood/jonas-30min (please pick a time this afternoon).

If that package looks fair I’ll send a 1-page addendum and a measurement checklist. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the calculation.
